statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump urging AI talks with China
statements.quote: While advanced AI may be new, engagement between two superpowers over a technology that poses an existential threat is not.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen, urging President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China to slow down and potentially mutually pause frontier AI development.

Called for a statewide moratorium on data center construction in Georgia after visiting the planned OpenAI site in Effingham County, citing transparency, utility bills, tax breaks and pollution (not risk from AI itself).
Questioned Federal Reserve Chair Warsh at a Banking Committee hearing about a possible AI bubble, retirement savings and worker representation on the Fed's AI task force.
Released a video after AI-generated fake posts about his health, calling for labelling of AI content and for Congress to act.
grade_reason: The only evidence at A or B is the 23 September 2026 letter he co-signed, which calls AI a technology that poses an existential threat and names bioweapons and loss of control. No statement in his own individual words about catastrophic AI risk was found; his own remarks on AI are all level D.
notes: Eight web searches ran in total (the seven listed; the brief's six required topics are covered, plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act); none was refused. All four quotes were checked by script as exact continuous passages of the letter text on the Van Hollen page, downloaded directly. The second quote is a part of a longer sentence (the full sentence exceeds 300 characters); it starts mid-sentence after 'including by working with China to develop'. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing Warnock as a co-sponsor; the search results named only Sanders, Casar and some House members, and I did not check Congress.gov, so this is unconfirmed rather than a verified 'no'. No press release on warnock.senate.gov about the China letter turned up in the site search. His own remarks, left out of statements because they are level D and less substantial than the letter (wording as returned by a page-reading tool, not verified character for character): in the 16 September 2026 video release he said 'We must deal with issues related to safety and jobs' and 'We need guardrails. We need regulations.' about AI deepfakes; at the July 2026 Banking hearing he said AI 'has both promise and peril' in the context of an AI bubble and jobs. The hearing date (probably 15 July 2026) is not stated on the page. A reviewer may want to weigh that the A grade rests entirely on a co-signed letter.
